definition: Ought self is the version of oneself a person feels they should be. In self-discrepancy theory, a gap between the actual self and the ought self is one form of self-discrepancy that can motivate behavior aimed at reducing that gap.

reasons: The definition states that “ought self” is “the version of oneself a person feels they should be,” but the packet only refers to an “ought or wish to be” self within self-discrepancy theory and does not explicitly equate “ought self” with what a person feels they “should be.”

The definition claims the gap between actual self and ought self “is one form of self-discrepancy,” but the packet does not enumerate or label “one form” in that way; it only describes self-discrepancy in general terms (actual vs. ideal/ought) and its motivational role.

The definition links “reducing that gap” to motivating behavior; while the packet supports motivation to reduce the discrepancy between the actual self and the self one “ought or wish to be,” it does not specifically frame this as reducing “that gap” between “actual self” and “ought self” as stated in the definition.
